Fractional evolution solvers, rational-approximation operators, and temporal projection.

## Fractional diffusion equations on metric graphs

We analyze and numerically approximate solutions to fractional diffusion equations on metric graphs of the form
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:maineq}
\tag{1}
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
    \partial_t u(s,t) + \nu(\kappa^2 - \Delta_\Gamma)^{\alpha/2} u(s,t) &= f(s,t), && \quad (s,t) \in \Gamma \times (0, T), \\
    u(s,0) &= u_0(s), && \quad s \in \Gamma,
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
with $u(\cdot,t)$ satisfying the Kirchhoff vertex conditions
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:Kcond}
\tag{2}
   \mathcal{K} =  \left\{\phi\in C(\Gamma)\;\middle|\; \forall v\in \mathcal{V}:\; \sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}_v}\partial_e \phi(v)=0 \right\}.
\end{equation}
The diffusion coefficient $\nu>0$ is fixed independently of the discretization.
Here $\Gamma = (\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E})$ is a metric graph, $\kappa>0$, $\alpha\in(0,2]$ determines the smoothness of $u(\cdot,t)$, $\Delta_{\Gamma}$ is the so-called Kirchhoff--Laplacian, and $f:\Gamma\times (0,T)\to\mathbb{R}$ and $u_0: \Gamma \to \mathbb{R}$ are fixed functions, called right-hand side and initial condition, respectively.

## Numerical Scheme {#num_scheme}

Let $\alpha\in(0,2]$ and $U_h^\tau$ denote the sequence of approximations of the solution to the weak form of problem \eqref{eq:maineq} at each time step on a mesh indexed by $h$. The scheme computes $U_h^{\tau}\subset V_h$, which solves
\begin{equation}
    \left\{
\begin{aligned}
    \langle\delta U_h^{k+1},\phi\rangle + \nu\mathfrak{a}(
        U_h^{k+1},\phi) &= \langle f^{k+1},\phi\rangle, \quad\forall\phi\in V_h,\quad k=0,\dots, N-1, \\
    U^0_h &= P_hu_0, 
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
where $f^{k+1} = \displaystyle\dfrac{1}{\tau}\int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}}f(t)dt$. The above expression can be equivalently written as
\begin{equation}
    \left\{
\begin{aligned}
    \langle\dfrac{U_h^{k+1} - U_h^{k}}{\tau},\phi\rangle + \nu\mathfrak{a}(
        U_h^{k+1},\phi) &= \langle f^{k+1},\phi\rangle, \quad\forall\phi\in V_h,\quad k=0,\dots, N-1, \\
    U^0_h &= P_hu_0, 
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
or
\begin{equation}
\label{system:fully_discrete_scheme}
\tag{3}
    \left\{
\begin{aligned}
    \langle U_h^{k+1},\phi\rangle + \tau\nu\mathfrak{a}(
        U_h^{k+1},\phi) &= \langle U_h^{k},\phi\rangle + \tau\langle f^{k+1},\phi\rangle, \quad\forall\phi\in V_h,\quad k=0,\dots, N-1, \\
    U^0_h &= P_hu_0.
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}

At each time step $t_k$, the finite element solution $U_h^k\in V_h$ to \eqref{system:fully_discrete_scheme} can be expressed as a linear combination of the basis functions  $\{\psi^i_h\}_{i=1}^{N_h}$ introduced in the [Preliminaries](preliminaries.html#fem-basis) page, namely, 
\begin{align}
\label{num_sol}
\tag{4}
    U_h^k(s) =  \sum_{i=1}^{N_h}u_i^k\psi^i_h(s), \;s\in\Gamma.
\end{align}

Replacing \eqref{num_sol} into \eqref{system:fully_discrete_scheme} yields the following system
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{j=1}^{N_h}u_j^{k+1}[(\psi_h^j,\psi_h^i)_{L_2(\Gamma)}+ \tau\nu\mathfrak{a}(\psi_h^j,\psi_h^i)] = \sum_{j=1}^{N_h}u_j^{k}(\psi_h^j,\psi_h^i)_{L_2(\Gamma)}+\tau( f^{k+1},\psi_h^i)_{L_2(\Gamma)},\quad i = 1,\dots, N_h.
\end{align*}
In matrix notation,
\begin{align}
\label{diff_eq_discrete}
    (\mathbf{C}+\tau\nu \mathbf{L}^{\alpha/2})\mathbf{U}^{k+1} = \mathbf{C}\mathbf{U}^k+\tau \mathbf{F}^{k+1},
\end{align}
or by introducing the scaling parameter $\kappa^2>0$,
\begin{align}
    (\mathbf{C}+\tau\nu (\kappa^2)^{\alpha/2}(\mathbf{L}/\kappa^2)^{\alpha/2})\mathbf{U}^{k+1} = \mathbf{C}\mathbf{U}^k+\tau \mathbf{F}^{k+1},
\end{align}
where $\mathbf{C}$ has entries $\mathbf{C}_{i,j} = (\psi_h^i,\psi_h^j)_{L_2(\Gamma)}$, $\mathbf{L}^{\alpha/2}$ has entries $\mathfrak{a}(\psi_h^i,\psi_h^j)$, $\mathbf{U}^k$ has components $u_j^k$, and $\mathbf{F}^k$ has components $( f^{k},\psi_h^i)_{L_2(\Gamma)}$. Applying $(\mathbf{L}/\kappa^2)^{-\alpha/2}$ to both sides yields
\begin{equation}
((\mathbf{L}/\kappa^2)^{-\alpha/2}\mathbf{C}+\tau\nu (\kappa^2)^{\alpha/2}\mathbf{I})\mathbf{U}^{k+1} = (\mathbf{L}/\kappa^2)^{-\alpha/2}(\mathbf{C}\mathbf{U}^k+\tau \mathbf{F}^{k+1}).
\end{equation}
The matrix studies use rSPDE's BRASIL coefficients at $\beta=\alpha/2$.
In the normalized spectral variable $y=\lambda/\kappa^2$, they define
\[
S_m(y)=d_m+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\rho_j(y-\eta_j)^{-1}\approx y^{-\beta},
\qquad d_m\geq0,\quad\rho_j>0,\quad\eta_j<0.
\]
Equivalently, $B_m(x)=S_m(1/x)$ directly approximates $x^\beta$ with
numerator and denominator degrees $(m,m)$. The source poles and residues
are converted to those of the backward Euler transfer function
\[
H_m(y)=\frac{S_m(y)}{S_m(y)+\tau\nu\kappa^{2\beta}}
=r_\tau+\sum_{n=1}^{m}a_n(y-z_n)^{-1},
\qquad r_\tau=\frac{d_m}{d_m+\tau\nu\kappa^{2\beta}}.
\]
The combined denominator's roots are bracketed between the negative
source poles; no polynomial coefficient expansion is needed.
With $L_h$ represented by $\mathbf C^{-1}\mathbf L$, the matrix update is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:final_scheme2}
\mathbf U^{k+1}=\mathbf C^{-1}\left(r_\tau\mathbf I+
\sum_{n=1}^{m}a_n(\mathbf L\mathbf C^{-1}/\kappa^2-z_n\mathbf I)^{-1}\right)
(\mathbf C\mathbf U^k+\tau\mathbf F^{k+1}).
\end{equation}
Since $(\mathbf L\mathbf C^{-1}/\kappa^2-z_n\mathbf I)^{-1}
=\mathbf C(\mathbf L/\kappa^2-z_n\mathbf C)^{-1}$, this becomes
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:final_scheme3}
\mathbf U^{k+1}=\left(r_\tau\mathbf C^{-1}+
\sum_{n=1}^{m}a_n(\mathbf L/\kappa^2-z_n\mathbf C)^{-1}\right)
(\mathbf C\mathbf U^k+\tau\mathbf F^{k+1}).
\end{equation}
The constant term is retained. All terms still use sparse solves with
cached Cholesky factors; $\beta=1$ uses ordinary backward Euler exactly.

## Numerical implementation {#num_implementation}

The shared `fun/brasil_coefficients.R` reads `m_brasil<m>t` from rSPDE,
using an exact exponent row when available and linear interpolation otherwise.
It also evaluates $S_m$ and constructs the time-step partial fractions.

The following root-table helpers are retained only for the optional
legacy `fractional_roots` interface; the three BRASIL studies do not use them.

### Function `my.get.roots()`

For each rational order $m$ (1,2,3,4) and smoothness parameter $\beta$ (= $\alpha/2$ with $\alpha$ between 0.5 and 2), function `my.get.roots()` (adapted from the `rSPDE` package) returns $\texttt{factor} = \dfrac{c_m}{b_{m+1}}$, and the roots $\{r_{1i}\}_{i=1}^m$ and $\{r_{2j}\}_{j=1}^{m+1}$.

```{r}
# Function to compute the roots and factor for the rational approximation
my.get.roots <- function(m, # rational order, m = 1, 2, 3, or 4
                         beta # smoothness parameter, beta = alpha/2 with alpha between 0.5 and 2
                         ) {
  m1table <- rSPDE:::m1table
  m2table <- rSPDE:::m2table
  m3table <- rSPDE:::m3table
  m4table <- rSPDE:::m4table
  mt <- get(paste0("m", m, "table"))
  rb <- rep(0, m + 1)
  rc <- rep(0, m)
  if(m == 1) {
    rc = approx(mt$beta, mt[[paste0("rc")]], beta)$y
  } else {
    rc = sapply(1:m, function(i) {
      approx(mt$beta, mt[[paste0("rc.", i)]], beta)$y
    })
  }
  rb = sapply(1:(m+1), function(i) {
    approx(mt$beta, mt[[paste0("rb.", i)]], xout = beta)$y
  })
  factor = approx(mt$beta, mt$factor, xout = beta)$y
  return(list(pl_roots = rb, # roots \{r_{2j}\}_{j=1}^{m+1}
              pr_roots = rc, # roots \{r_{1i}\}_{i=1}^m
              factor = factor # this is c_m/b_{m+1}
              ))
}
```

### Function `poly.from.roots()`

Function `poly.from.roots()` computes the coefficients of a polynomial from its roots.

```{r}
# Function to compute polynomial coefficients from roots
poly.from.roots <- function(roots) {
  coef <- 1
  for (r in roots) {coef <- convolve(coef, c(1, -r), type = "open")}
  return(coef) # returned in increasing order like a+bx+cx^2+...
}
```

### Function `compute.partial.fraction.param()`

Given the legacy root/factor coefficients, `time_step`$=\tau$, and
`scaling`$=\nu\kappa^{2\beta}$, `compute.partial.fraction.param()` computes
the root-based time-step partial fractions. The BRASIL path instead uses
`brasil_partial_fractions()`.

```{r}
# Function to compute the parameters for the partial fraction decomposition
compute.partial.fraction.param <- function(factor, # c_m/b_{m+1}
                                           pr_roots, # roots \{r_{1i}\}_{i=1}^m
                                           pl_roots, # roots \{r_{2j}\}_{j=1}^{m+1}
                                           time_step, # \tau
                                           scaling, # diffusion * kappa^(2*beta)
                                           stable = FALSE
                                           ) {
  if (stable) {
    direct_polynomial <- function(roots) {
      coefficients <- 1
      for (r in roots) coefficients <- c(-r * coefficients, 0) + c(0, coefficients)
      coefficients
    }
    strength <- (scaling*time_step)/factor
    if (!is.finite(strength) || strength <= 0)
      stop("Invalid or underflowed scaled time step in the rational update.")
    pr_coef <- c(0, direct_polynomial(pr_roots))
    pl_coef <- direct_polynomial(pl_roots)
    factor_pr_coef <- pr_coef
    pr_plus_pl_coef <- factor_pr_coef + strength * pl_coef
    #res <- gsignal::residue(factor_pr_coef, pr_plus_pl_coef)
    # Coefficients passed here are in descending powers.
    # polyroot() expects ascending powers.
    p <- polyroot(rev(pr_plus_pl_coef))

    # Verify that these poles are numerically real and negative.
    stopifnot(
      all(abs(Im(p)) <= 1e-10 * pmax(1, abs(Re(p)))),
      all(Re(p) < 0)
    )
    p <- Re(p)

    derivative <- function(roots, x) sum(vapply(seq_along(roots), function(j)
      -roots[j]*prod(1-roots[-j]*x), numeric(1)))
    # At a pole P=-strength*Q: use that identity instead of evaluating the
    # nearly zero numerator. Products/derivatives retain the root representation.
    r <- vapply(p, function(x) {
      -strength*prod(1-pl_roots*x)/
        (derivative(pr_roots, x)+strength*derivative(pl_roots, x))
    }, numeric(1))
    if (length(p) != length(pl_roots) || any(!is.finite(r)) || any(r <= 0))
      stop("Unstable rational update: residues must be finite and positive.")
    # Guard against a misleading real-pole result with inaccurate reconstruction.
    z <- 10^seq(0, 12, length.out = 65L)
    P <- vapply(z, function(x) prod(1-pr_roots*x), numeric(1))
    Q <- vapply(z, function(x) prod(1-pl_roots*x), numeric(1))
    expected <- P/(P+strength*Q)
    reconstructed <- rowSums(vapply(seq_along(p), function(j) r[j]/(z-p[j]), numeric(length(z))))
    if (any(!is.finite(reconstructed)) || max(abs(reconstructed-expected)) > 5e-9)
      stop("Unstable rational update: partial-fraction reconstruction failed.")

    res <- list(r = r, p = p, k = numeric(0))
    return(list(r = res$r, # residues \{a_k\}_{k=1}^{m+1}
                p = res$p, # poles \{p_k\}_{k=1}^{m+1}
                k = res$k # remainder r
                ))
  }
  pr_coef <- c(0, poly.from.roots(pr_roots))
  pl_coef <- poly.from.roots(pl_roots)
  factor_pr_coef <- pr_coef
  pr_plus_pl_coef <- factor_pr_coef + ((scaling * time_step)/factor) * pl_coef
  #res <- gsignal::residue(factor_pr_coef, pr_plus_pl_coef)
  # Coefficients passed here are in descending powers.
  # polyroot() expects ascending powers.
  p <- polyroot(rev(pr_plus_pl_coef))
  
  # Verify that these poles are numerically real and negative.
  stopifnot(
    all(abs(Im(p)) <= 1e-10 * pmax(1, abs(Re(p)))),
    all(Re(p) < 0)
  )
  p <- Re(p)
  
  eval_poly <- function(coef, x) {
    Reduce(function(value, a) value * x + a, coef, init = 0)
  }
  
  r <- vapply(seq_along(p), function(j) {
    eval_poly(factor_pr_coef, p[j]) /
      (pr_plus_pl_coef[1] * prod(p[j] - p[-j]))
  }, numeric(1))
  
  res <- list(r = r, p = p, k = numeric(0))
  return(list(r = res$r, # residues \{a_k\}_{k=1}^{m+1}
              p = res$p, # poles \{p_k\}_{k=1}^{m+1}
              k = res$k # remainder r
              ))
}
```

### Function `my.fractional.operators.frac()`

The default coefficient source is rSPDE BRASIL at exponent `beta` and
order `m`. The operator retains the shifted sparse matrices and cached
Cholesky factors, adding a mass-matrix factor for the constant remainder.
`diffusion` multiplies the fractional power; meshes and time steps are unchanged.
The optional `fractional_roots` list preserves the legacy root-based interface.

```{r}
# Function to compute the fractional operator
my.fractional.operators.frac <- function(L, beta, C, scale.factor, m = 1,
                                         time_step, diffusion = 1,
                                         fractional_roots = NULL) {
  stopifnot(length(diffusion) == 1L, is.finite(diffusion), diffusion > 0,
            length(time_step) == 1L, is.finite(time_step), time_step > 0,
            length(beta) == 1L, is.finite(beta), beta > 0, beta <= 1,
            length(scale.factor) == 1L, is.finite(scale.factor), scale.factor > 0)
  L <- L / scale.factor
  if (beta == 1) {
    L <- L * scale.factor^beta
    lhs <- C + time_step * diffusion * L
    return(list(C = C, L = L, m = m, beta = beta, diffusion = diffusion,
                LHS = lhs, factorization = Matrix::Cholesky(
                  Matrix::forceSymmetric(lhs), LDL = FALSE)))
  }
  scaling <- diffusion * scale.factor^beta
  if (is.null(fractional_roots)) {
    coefficients <- brasil_coefficients(m, beta)
    poles_rs_k <- brasil_partial_fractions(coefficients, time_step, scaling)
  } else {
    # Retain the optional legacy root-coefficient interface.
    roots <- fractional_roots
    values <- c(roots$pr_roots, roots$pl_roots)
    stopifnot(length(roots$factor) == 1L, is.finite(roots$factor), roots$factor > 0,
              length(roots$pr_roots) == m, length(roots$pl_roots) == m + 1L,
              is.numeric(values), !is.complex(values), all(is.finite(values)), all(values < 0))
    poles_rs_k <- compute.partial.fraction.param(roots$factor, roots$pr_roots,
      roots$pl_roots, time_step, scaling, stable = TRUE)
  }
  partial_fraction_terms <- lapply(poles_rs_k$p, function(p) L - p * C)
  remainder <- if (length(poles_rs_k$k)) poles_rs_k$k else 0
  list(C = C, L = L, m = m, beta = beta, diffusion = diffusion,
       partial_fraction_terms = partial_fraction_terms,
       residues = poles_rs_k$r, poles = poles_rs_k$p, remainder = remainder,
       mass_factor = if (remainder != 0) Matrix::Cholesky(
         Matrix::forceSymmetric(C), LDL = FALSE) else NULL,
       factorizations = lapply(partial_fraction_terms, function(A)
         Matrix::Cholesky(Matrix::forceSymmetric(A), LDL = FALSE)))
}

```

### Function `my.solver.frac()`

Given the object returned by `my.fractional.operators.frac()` and a vector `v`, function `my.solver.frac()` solves the linear \eqref{eq:final_scheme2} for the vector `v`. If `beta = 1`, it solves the system directly; otherwise, it uses the partial fraction decomposition and reuses the stored Cholesky factors. Older operator objects without stored factors remain supported.

```{r}
# Function to solve the iteration
my.solver.frac <- function(obj, v) {
  if (obj$beta == 1) {
    return(if (!is.null(obj$factorization))
      solve(obj$factorization, v, system = "A") else solve(obj$LHS, v))
  }
  partial_fraction_terms <- obj$partial_fraction_terms
  residues <- obj$residues
  output <- v * 0
  if (!is.null(obj$remainder) && obj$remainder != 0) {
    mass_solved <- if (!is.null(obj$mass_factor))
      solve(obj$mass_factor, v, system = "A") else solve(obj$C, v)
    output <- obj$remainder * mass_solved
  }
  for (i in seq_along(residues)) {
    solved <- if (!is.null(obj$factorizations)) {
      solve(obj$factorizations[[i]], v, system = "A")
    } else solve(partial_fraction_terms[[i]], v)
    output <- output + residues[i] * solved
  }
  return(output)
}

```


### Function `solve_fractional_evolution()`

Given the fractional operator object `my_op_frac`, a time step `time_step`, a sequence of time points `time_seq`, an initial value `val_at_0`, and the right-hand side matrix `RHST`, function `solve_fractional_evolution()` computes the solution to the fractional diffusion equation at each time step using scheme \eqref{eq:final_scheme2}.


```{r}
solve_fractional_evolution <- function(my_op_frac, time_step, time_seq, val_at_0, RHST) {
  CC <- my_op_frac$C
  SOL <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(CC), ncol = length(time_seq))
  SOL[, 1] <- val_at_0
  for (k in 1:(length(time_seq) - 1)) {
    rhs <- CC %*% SOL[, k] + time_step * RHST[, k + 1]
    SOL[, k + 1] <- as.matrix(my.solver.frac(my_op_frac, rhs))
  }
  return(SOL)
}
```

### Function `estimate_error_memory()`

Estimate the memory associated with error accumulation before allocating a reference time grid or running the solver. For compressed error, supply `n_exact_modes`; block matrices then have that many rows instead of the reference spatial dimension. The sparse reference metric and projection setup are resident objects excluded from the block estimate and can be included through `baseline_gib`. Supply the number of reference spatial nodes, the number of positive-time reference samples (excluding $t=0$), and one or more requested block counts. The estimator uses scalar arithmetic and allocates only its small result table. `n_solver_steps` may contain the step counts of multiple stored solver grids, as in the temporal-convergence experiment.

`matrix_gib` is the payload of one dense double-precision block matrix. `block_workspace_gib` allows for `matrix_copies` such matrices (six by default) plus approximately 128 bytes per sample for block indices and other temporal work vectors. `time_vectors_gib` counts one full reference time vector and, for every supplied solver grid, its time vector and forcing-average vector. Increasing the number of blocks reduces block workspace, but not those full time vectors. The effective block count is capped at the number of positive-time samples, just as in the solver.

`estimated_gib` sums these modeled quantities and the optional `baseline_gib` allowance for other resident objects. With the default `baseline_gib = 0`, graph/FEM objects, spatial modes, solver matrices and factorizations, other R-session memory, and temporary allocations during grid/forcing construction are excluded. The six-matrix allowance is a planning assumption, not a measured peak or a guaranteed upper bound: custom exact-solution callbacks and R's garbage collector can change the actual peak. All sizes use GiB ($2^{30}$ bytes).

```{r}
estimate_error_memory <- function(
    n_reference_nodes, n_reference_samples, n_blocks,
    n_solver_steps = numeric(0), matrix_copies = 6,
    baseline_gib = 0, n_exact_modes = NULL) {

  positive_counts <- function(x) {
    is.numeric(x) && length(x) > 0L &&
      all(is.finite(x)) && all(x >= 1) && all(x == floor(x))
  }
  stopifnot(
    positive_counts(n_reference_nodes), length(n_reference_nodes) == 1L,
    positive_counts(n_reference_samples), length(n_reference_samples) == 1L,
    positive_counts(n_blocks),
    is.numeric(n_solver_steps),
    length(n_solver_steps) == 0L || positive_counts(n_solver_steps),
    is.numeric(matrix_copies), length(matrix_copies) == 1L,
    is.finite(matrix_copies), matrix_copies >= 1,
    is.numeric(baseline_gib), length(baseline_gib) == 1L,
    is.finite(baseline_gib), baseline_gib >= 0
  )

  if (!is.null(n_exact_modes)) stopifnot(positive_counts(n_exact_modes),
                                         length(n_exact_modes) == 1L)

  # Promote counts before multiplication to avoid integer overflow.
  samples <- as.double(n_reference_samples)
  blocks <- pmin(as.double(n_blocks), samples)
  per_block <- ceiling(samples / blocks)
  gib <- 1024^3
  block_rows <- if (is.null(n_exact_modes)) n_reference_nodes else n_exact_modes
  matrix_bytes <- 8 * as.double(block_rows) * per_block
  block_bytes <- matrix_copies * matrix_bytes + 128 * per_block
  time_bytes <- 8 * (samples + 1 +
    2 * sum(as.double(n_solver_steps) + 1))

  data.frame(
    error_method = if (is.null(n_exact_modes)) "reference" else "compressed",
    requested_blocks = as.double(n_blocks),
    n_blocks = blocks,
    samples_per_block = per_block,
    matrix_gib = matrix_bytes / gib,
    block_workspace_gib = block_bytes / gib,
    time_vectors_gib = time_bytes / gib,
    baseline_gib = baseline_gib,
    estimated_gib = (block_bytes + time_bytes) / gib + baseline_gib
  )
}
```

### Reference-grid error compression

The numerical solution remains the full FEM vector, advanced at every
backward Euler step. Only the reference-error calculation is compressed.
Let $E$ contain the reference-node values of the exact spatial modes and
let $c(t)$ contain their analytic coefficients. For the same interpolation
matrix $\Psi$ and reference mass matrix $C^\star$ as before, define
\[
M=\Psi^\top C^\star\Psi,\quad B=\Psi^\top C^\star E,\quad
MZ=B,\quad R=(E-\Psi Z)^\top C^\star(E-\Psi Z),\quad
H=E^\top C^\star E.
\]
The normal equations give $\Psi^\top C^\star(E-\Psi Z)=0$, hence
\[
\|Ec-\Psi U\|_{C^\star}^2
=\|U-Zc\|_M^2+c^\top Rc.
\]
This is the original reference-matrix norm, with no assumptions about
uniform meshes or discrete eigenfunctions. `prepare_reference_error()`
performs the sparse projection once per spatial mesh. It constructs the
residual Gram matrix directly to avoid subtracting nearly equal Grams.

For reference samples in one solver interval, let $W=\sum_i w_i$,
$\bar c=W^{-1}\sum_iw_ic_i$, and
$V=\sum_iw_i(c_i-\bar c)(c_i-\bar c)^\top$. The same weighted error sum is
\[
W\|U^k-Z\bar c\|_M^2+W\bar c^\top R\bar c+
\operatorname{tr}(HV).
\]
All reference times and right-endpoint weights are preserved. Centered
moments are merged across blocks using the weighted covariance identity,
so a solver interval spanning several blocks still needs only one
solver-sized quadratic form. Every solver step is still advanced, even
when it contains no reference sample. `n_blocks` now controls small
coefficient blocks rather than reference-space matrices.

```{r}
prepare_reference_error <- function(Psi, reference_C, reference_basis) {
  E <- as.matrix(reference_basis)
  stopifnot(nrow(Psi) == nrow(reference_C), nrow(reference_C) == ncol(reference_C),
            nrow(E) == nrow(Psi), ncol(E) >= 1L, all(is.finite(E)))
  metric <- Matrix::forceSymmetric(as(
    Matrix::Matrix(Matrix::crossprod(Psi, reference_C %*% Psi), sparse = TRUE),
    "CsparseMatrix"))
  cross <- Matrix::crossprod(Psi, reference_C %*% E)
  factor <- Matrix::Cholesky(metric, LDL = FALSE)
  projection <- as.matrix(solve(factor, cross, system = "A"))
  residual <- E - as.matrix(Psi %*% projection)
  list(metric = metric, projection = projection,
       residual_gram = as.matrix(crossprod(residual, reference_C %*% residual)),
       exact_gram = as.matrix(crossprod(E, reference_C %*% E)))
}

reference_coefficient_moments <- function(coefficients, weights) {
  coefficients <- as.matrix(coefficients)
  stopifnot(nrow(coefficients) >= 1L, ncol(coefficients) == length(weights),
            length(weights) >= 1L, all(is.finite(coefficients)),
            all(is.finite(weights)), all(weights > 0))
  weight <- sum(weights)
  centered <- sweep(coefficients, 1L, coefficients[, 1L], `-`)
  shift <- as.numeric(centered %*% (weights / weight))
  deviations <- sweep(centered, 1L, shift, `-`)
  list(weight = weight, mean = coefficients[, 1L] + shift,
       scatter = tcrossprod(sweep(deviations, 2L, sqrt(weights), `*`)))
}

merge_reference_moments <- function(left, right) {
  if (is.null(left)) return(right)
  weight <- left$weight + right$weight
  delta <- right$mean - left$mean
  list(weight = weight, mean = left$mean + (right$weight / weight) * delta,
       scatter = left$scatter + right$scatter +
         (left$weight * (right$weight / weight)) * tcrossprod(delta))
}

reference_interval_error <- function(u, moments, projection) {
  delta <- as.numeric(u - projection$projection %*% moments$mean)
  metric_product <- as.numeric(projection$metric %*% delta)
  residual_product <- as.numeric(projection$residual_gram %*% moments$mean)
  variance_terms <- projection$exact_gram * moments$scatter
  value <- moments$weight * (sum(delta * metric_product) +
            sum(moments$mean * residual_product)) + sum(variance_terms)
  scale <- moments$weight * (sum(abs(delta * metric_product)) +
            sum(abs(moments$mean * residual_product))) + sum(abs(variance_terms))
  if (!is.finite(value) || value < -128 * .Machine$double.eps * scale)
    stop("Invalid compressed reference-grid squared error.")
  max(0, value)
}

solve_compressed_reference_error <- function(
    my_op_frac, time_step, time_seq, val_at_0, spatial_load, g_average,
    reference_times, coefficients_at_time, error_projection,
    n_blocks = 1000L, verbose = FALSE) {
  stopifnot(nrow(error_projection$metric) == length(val_at_0),
            ncol(error_projection$metric) == length(val_at_0),
            nrow(error_projection$projection) == length(val_at_0))
  n_modes <- ncol(error_projection$projection)
  stopifnot(identical(dim(error_projection$exact_gram), c(n_modes, n_modes)),
            identical(dim(error_projection$residual_gram), c(n_modes, n_modes)))
  n_samples <- length(reference_times) - 1L
  n_blocks <- min(n_blocks, n_samples)
  u <- as.numeric(val_at_0)
  spatial_load <- as.numeric(spatial_load)
  solver_step <- 0L
  active_step <- NULL
  moments <- NULL
  total <- compensation <- 0
  next_ref <- 2L
  started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  finish_interval <- function() {
    value <- reference_interval_error(u, moments, error_projection)
    adjusted <- value - compensation
    updated <- total + adjusted
    compensation <<- (updated - total) - adjusted
    total <<- updated
  }
  for (block in seq_len(n_blocks)) {
    last_ref <- if (block == n_blocks) length(reference_times) else
      1L + floor(block * n_samples / n_blocks)
    ids <- seq.int(next_ref, last_ref)
    times <- reference_times[ids]
    weights <- times - reference_times[ids - 1L]
    coefficients <- as.matrix(coefficients_at_time(times))
    stopifnot(nrow(coefficients) == n_modes, ncol(coefficients) == length(times),
              all(is.finite(coefficients)))
    runs <- rle(findInterval(times, time_seq, left.open = TRUE))
    first_column <- 1L
    for (run in seq_along(runs$values)) {
      target <- runs$values[run]
      if (is.null(active_step) || target != active_step) {
        if (!is.null(active_step)) finish_interval()
        while (solver_step < target) {
          solver_step <- solver_step + 1L
          rhs <- my_op_frac$C %*% u +
            time_step * spatial_load * g_average[solver_step + 1L]
          u <- as.numeric(my.solver.frac(my_op_frac, rhs))
        }
        active_step <- target
        moments <- NULL
      }
      last_column <- first_column + runs$lengths[run] - 1L
      columns <- seq.int(first_column, last_column)
      moments <- merge_reference_moments(moments, reference_coefficient_moments(
        coefficients[, columns, drop = FALSE], weights[columns]))
      first_column <- last_column + 1L
    }
    next_ref <- last_ref + 1L
    if (verbose) message(sprintf(
      "Compressed reference error: block %s/%s, %.1f%%, solver step %s/%s, %.2f s elapsed",
      block, n_blocks, 100 * (last_ref - 1L) / n_samples,
      solver_step, length(time_seq) - 1L, proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - started))
  }
  finish_interval()
  stopifnot(next_ref == length(reference_times) + 1L,
            solver_step == length(time_seq) - 1L)
  sqrt(total)
}
```

### Function `solve_fractional_evolution_error()`

Advance the numerical solution one step at a time and accumulate the reference-grid error without storing a space-time solution matrix. The separable forcing is supplied through a spatial load vector and its interval-averaged temporal factors. For each reference time in $(t_{k-1},t_k]$, compare the exact solution with the current iterate \(U_h^k\). The initial reference sample has zero weight, and subsequent samples use the right-endpoint weights \(t_j^\star-t_{j-1}^\star\).

The default `error_method = "reference"` retains the original accumulator.
Set `error_method = "compressed"`, supply `coefficients_at_time(t)`, and
prepare `error_projection` once per spatial mesh with `prepare_reference_error()`.
The compressed path preserves every reference time, endpoint weight, and
reference mass-matrix inner product; only its algebraic evaluation changes.
Diffusion is already included in `my_op_frac` and the exact decay rates,
so the forcing term below is never multiplied by it.

The callback `exact_at_time(t)` returns a matrix of exact solution values at the reference spatial nodes, with one column per supplied time. The parameter `n_blocks` divides the positive-time reference samples into that many approximately equal blocks, capped at the number of samples. Blocks may span multiple solver intervals; each sample uses the corresponding piecewise constant numerical state. Larger numbers of blocks reduce temporary memory use. Choosing at least as many blocks as reference samples gives one-at-a-time evaluation, for which a vector-valued callback is also accepted.

With `verbose = TRUE`, the function reports the initial block dimensions and approximate size of one dense matrix, followed by the completed block, percentage and sample count, current solver step, elapsed time, and estimated time remaining. The function returns the accumulated space-time error.

```{r}
solve_fractional_evolution_error <- function(
    my_op_frac, time_step, time_seq, val_at_0,
    spatial_load, g_average, Psi, reference_C,
    reference_times, exact_at_time = NULL, n_blocks = 1000L,
    verbose = FALSE, error_method = c("reference", "compressed"),
    reference_basis = NULL, coefficients_at_time = NULL, error_projection = NULL) {

  error_method <- match.arg(error_method)
  stopifnot(
    length(time_step) == 1L,
    is.finite(time_step), time_step > 0,
    length(time_seq) >= 2L,
    length(reference_times) >= 2L,
    all(is.finite(time_seq)),
    all(is.finite(reference_times)),
    all(diff(time_seq) > 0),
    all(diff(reference_times) > 0),
    reference_times[1] == time_seq[1],
    tail(reference_times, 1) == tail(time_seq, 1),
    length(g_average) == length(time_seq),
    length(val_at_0) == nrow(my_op_frac$C),
    length(spatial_load) == length(val_at_0),
    ncol(Psi) == length(val_at_0),
    nrow(Psi) == nrow(reference_C),
    nrow(reference_C) == ncol(reference_C),
    if (error_method == "reference") is.function(exact_at_time) else
      is.function(coefficients_at_time),
    length(n_blocks) == 1L,
    is.finite(n_blocks), n_blocks >= 1,
    n_blocks == floor(n_blocks),
    is.logical(verbose), length(verbose) == 1L, !is.na(verbose)
  )

  if (error_method == "compressed") {
    if (is.null(error_projection)) {
      if (is.null(reference_basis)) stop("Compressed error needs reference_basis or error_projection.")
      error_projection <- prepare_reference_error(Psi, reference_C, reference_basis)
    }
    return(solve_compressed_reference_error(
      my_op_frac, time_step, time_seq, val_at_0, spatial_load, g_average,
      reference_times, coefficients_at_time, error_projection, n_blocks, verbose))
  }

  n_samples <- length(reference_times) - 1L
  n_blocks <- min(n_blocks, n_samples)
  samples_per_block <- n_samples / n_blocks
  n_steps <- length(time_seq) - 1L
  u <- as.numeric(val_at_0)
  spatial_load <- as.numeric(spatial_load)
  solver_step <- 0L
  projected_step <- -1L
  u_ref <- NULL
  next_ref <- 2L
  error_sum <- 0
  started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]

  if (verbose) {
    message(sprintf(
      "Error accumulation: %s reference samples in %s blocks; up to %s samples/block (%.2f GiB per dense matrix).",
      format(n_samples, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
      format(n_blocks, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
      format(ceiling(samples_per_block), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
      8 * nrow(reference_C) * ceiling(samples_per_block) / 1024^3
    ))
  }

  for (block in seq_len(n_blocks)) {
    last_ref <- if (block == n_blocks) {
      length(reference_times)
    } else {
      1L + floor(block * samples_per_block)
    }
    ids <- seq.int(next_ref, last_ref)
    times <- reference_times[ids]
    target_steps <- findInterval(times, time_seq, left.open = TRUE)
    runs <- rle(target_steps)

    error <- as.matrix(exact_at_time(times))
    stopifnot(
      nrow(error) == nrow(reference_C),
      ncol(error) == length(ids)
    )

    first_column <- 1L
    for (run in seq_along(runs$values)) {
      target <- runs$values[run]
      while (solver_step < target) {
        solver_step <- solver_step + 1L
        rhs <- my_op_frac$C %*% u +
          time_step * spatial_load * g_average[solver_step + 1L]
        u <- as.numeric(my.solver.frac(my_op_frac, rhs))
      }

      if (projected_step != target) {
        u_ref <- as.numeric(Psi %*% u)
        projected_step <- target
      }

      last_column <- first_column + runs$lengths[run] - 1L
      columns <- seq.int(first_column, last_column)
      error[, columns] <- error[, columns, drop = FALSE] - u_ref
      first_column <- last_column + 1L
    }

    squared <- colSums(error * (reference_C %*% error))
    weights <- times - reference_times[ids - 1L]
    error_sum <- error_sum + sum(weights * squared)
    rm(error)
    next_ref <- last_ref + 1L

    if (verbose) {
      processed <- last_ref - 1L
      elapsed <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - started
      remaining <- elapsed * (n_samples / processed - 1)
      message(sprintf(
        "Block %s/%s | %.1f%% | %s/%s samples | solver step %s/%s | elapsed %.1f min | ETA %.1f min",
        block, n_blocks, 100 * processed / n_samples,
        format(processed, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
        format(n_samples, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
        solver_step, n_steps, elapsed / 60, remaining / 60
      ))
    }
  }

  stopifnot(next_ref == length(reference_times) + 1L,
            solver_step == n_steps)
  sqrt(error_sum)
}
```

### Function `construct_piecewise_projection()` {#construct_piecewise_projection}

Given a matrix `projected_U_approx` with approximated values at discrete time points, a sequence of time points `time_seq`, and an extended sequence of time points `overkill_time_seq`, function `construct_piecewise_projection()` constructs a piecewise constant projection of the approximated values over the extended time sequence.

```{r}
# Function to construct a piecewise constant projection of approximated values
# construct_piecewise_projection <- function(projected_U_approx, time_seq, overkill_time_seq) {
#   projected_U_piecewise <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(projected_U_approx), ncol = length(overkill_time_seq))
  
#   # Assign value at t = 0
#   projected_U_piecewise[, which(overkill_time_seq == 0)] <- projected_U_approx[, 1]
  
#   # Assign values for intervals (t_{k-1}, t_k]
#   for (k in 2:length(time_seq)) {
#     idxs <- which(overkill_time_seq > time_seq[k - 1] & overkill_time_seq <= time_seq[k])
#     projected_U_piecewise[, idxs] <- projected_U_approx[, k]
#   }
  
#   return(projected_U_piecewise)
# }
construct_piecewise_projection <- function(
    projected_U_approx, time_seq, overkill_time_seq) {

  stopifnot(
    length(time_seq) >= 2L,
    ncol(projected_U_approx) == length(time_seq),
    all(is.finite(time_seq)),
    all(diff(time_seq) > 0),
    all(is.finite(overkill_time_seq)),
    all(overkill_time_seq >= time_seq[1]),
    all(overkill_time_seq <= tail(time_seq, 1))
  )

  columns <- findInterval(
    overkill_time_seq,
    time_seq,
    left.open = TRUE
  ) + 1L

  projected_U_approx[, columns, drop = FALSE]
}
```

```{r}
make_time_grid <- function(T_final, target_step) {
  stopifnot(
    length(T_final) == 1L, is.finite(T_final), T_final > 0,
    length(target_step) == 1L,
    is.finite(target_step), target_step > 0
  )
  N <- ceiling(T_final / target_step)
  time_step <- T_final / N
  time_seq <- seq(0, T_final, length.out = N + 1)
  
  return(list(N = N, time_step = time_step, time_seq = time_seq))
}
```

The next function computes

\[
\overline g_k
=\frac1\tau\int_{t_{k-1}}^{t_k}g(t)\,dt
=\frac{A[\cos(\omega t_{k-1})-\cos(\omega t_k)]}{\omega\tau}.
\]
To avoid subtracting nearly equal cosines, we use the equivalent formula
\[
\overline g_k
=A\sin\!\left(\omega\frac{t_{k-1}+t_k}{2}\right)
\frac{\sin(\omega\tau/2)}{\omega\tau/2}.
\]

```{r}
average_sine_forcing <- function(time_seq, A = 1, omega = pi) {
  dt <- diff(time_seq)

  stopifnot(
    length(time_seq) >= 2L,
    all(is.finite(time_seq)),
    all(dt > 0)
  )

  midpoint <- head(time_seq, -1) + dt/2
  z <- omega * dt/2

  # sin(z)/z, with its limiting value at z = 0.
  sinc_z <- rep(1, length(z))
  nonzero <- z != 0
  sinc_z[nonzero] <- sin(z[nonzero]) / z[nonzero]

  averages <- A * sin(omega * midpoint) * sinc_z

  # First entry is unused by the evolution solver.
  c(0, averages)
}
```
